page: Vultr vbm-64c-1536gb-amd is a bare metal server configured with an AMD EPYC 9354 processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 64 physical cores and 128 vCPUs with dedicated allocation, operating at a base clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 1536.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, providing 12.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage consists of a 480 GB NVMe SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present on this instance.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance across multiple compute and memory metrics. The server achieves a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 203240.04 and a Passmark CPU score of 117661.25, placing it in the top 10% of tested systems. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, with read-only small block cached speeds reaching 10045.41 GB/sec and large block uncached write speeds at 329.05 GB/sec. Database operations are highly efficient, as demonstrated by a Passmark database score of 33566.39 and a Redis SET throughput of 170.67 million operations per second. However, single-threaded operations show average performance, with gzip compression at 29.77 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 13.71 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this bare metal server offers high resource density, combining massive DDR5 memory capacity with 128 dedicated execution threads. This profile minimizes virtualization overhead and makes it highly suitable for memory-intensive and parallelized workloads. Tradeoffs include a relatively small local storage capacity of 480 GB NVMe SSD relative to the massive compute and memory footprint, meaning external storage may be required for data-heavy applications. Recommended workloads include large-scale database hosting, in-memory caching, high-throughput web serving, and multi-threaded data processing tasks.

This server is highly suited for memory-intensive databases, in-memory caching, and concurrent data processing applications.
